result: Elba is a novel developmentally restricted boundary factor consisting of a hetero-tripartite protein complex (Elba1, Elba2, and Elba3). Elba1 and Elba2 share a conserved C-terminal BEN domain, while Elba3 has no obvious conserved domains but is encoded by a gene closely linked to elba1.

The structural characterization (C23-C25) is supported by sequence analysis and genomic location data. Multiple independent lines of evidence converge on this conclusion.

result: All three Elba proteins are required to reconstitute DNA binding activity in vitro. DNA binding depends on the BEN domains in Elba1 and Elba2, while Elba3 mediates complex assembly by interacting with the N-terminal domains of Elba1 and Elba2. The reconstituted complex exhibits the same sequence specificity as the endogenous factor.

result: All three Elba proteins are present in the endogenous Elba complex in 0–6 hr nuclear extracts and are required for chromatin domain boundary function in vivo. RNAi knockdown of any of the three Elba proteins compromises insulating activity, while knockdown of the related protein Insv has no effect.

result: Elba binding and insulator activity are developmentally restricted to early embryogenesis because elba1 and elba3 are mid-blastula transition genes with transient expression, while elba2 is maternally deposited and expressed throughout development. Elba proteins are associated with Fab-7 in 2–5 hr embryos but not in 9–12 hr embryos.

result: Elba confers the early embryonic insulator activity of the pHS1 sub-element of Fab-7 through direct binding to an 8-bp recognition sequence (CCAATAAG). Mutations in this sequence compromise insulator activity, while multimerization of the sequence is sufficient to confer insulating activity.

result: A cross-affinity purification strategy identified three proteins (Elba1, Elba2, Elba3) substantially enriched in the wild-type fraction. The elba genes show interesting genomic organization with elba1/elba3 and elba2/insv forming linked pairs.

result: The use of developmentally restricted factors like Elba at Fab-7 may reflect the need to optimize boundary combinations with neighboring elements, as boundaries function in pairwise combinations that are context-dependent and developmentally regulated. result: Chromatin boundaries subdivide chromosomes into functionally autonomous domains and have diverse functions including enhancer-blocking, silencer-blocking, and long-range interactions. The regulatory domain landscape is more dynamic than previously thought and can be redefined during development and disease.
